title: Rapid capacity mosaic - cross-team quick snapshot
body:
Purpose:
A minimal, shared spreadsheet-style snapshot to align engineering, SRE, and solutions on an expected mid-Nov burst (marketing campaign + pilot rollouts). Not exhaustive — lightweight inputs only so we can 1) estimate incremental GPU-hours, 2) surface pinch points, and 3) collect quick asks for Dedicated/Private capacity adjustments.

Usage notes (TL;DR):
- Fill only the 'Expected burst GPUs' column and any quick asks.
- If you have committed Dedicated capacity, list it under 'Reserved GPUs'.
- If uncertain, mark with ~ and put a short note in the Quick Ask column.

Snapshot table (pipe-separated for quick paste into sheets):
Team | Service / Workload | Reserved GPUs | Expected burst GPUs | Est additional GPU-hrs/day | Priority | Owner | Quick ask / blocker
Serving-runtime | hosted-inference-prod | 8 | 14 | 144 | P0 | Jonah Park | Need temporary burst quota from Dedicated pool (JIRA-1228)
Solutions SE | demo-benchmarks | 0 | 4 | 32 | P1 | Marina Lopez | Borrow 1 GPU for bench jobs; coordinate slot schedule
Platform-engineering | canary-rollout | 2 | 6 | 48 | P0 | Ethan Brooks | Request canary capacity window 11/10-11/15; auto-scale policy tweak
Observability | tracing-ingest | 1 | 2 | 16 | P2 | Priya Desai | Monitor only; may throttle non-prod traces
Private-PS | enterprise-pilot | 0 | 12 | 96 | P0 | Sophia Ramos | Customer pilot needs isolated nodes; estimate 12 GPUs for 7 days
SRE | background-evals | 1 | 3 | 24 | P1 | Carlos Mendez | Stagger eval jobs; ask for GPU scheduling priority

Assumptions used for quick math:
- Est additional GPU-hrs/day = (Expected burst GPUs - Reserved GPUs) * 12 hours/day run average (conservative for burst windows).
- Cost proxy = $2.50 per GPU-hour (internal quick estimate; use billing team for exact).
- Duration assumed for planning: 7 days unless noted in Quick ask.

Quick cost headcount (very rough):
- Total estimated additional GPU-hrs/day = 360 hrs/day (sum of rows above).
- Per-day incremental cost ≈ 360 * $2.50 = $900/day.
- For a 7-day burst ≈ $6,300 incremental compute.
(Flag: if Private nodes or Dedicated committed capacity used, billing may be different; this is just a planning proxy.)

Action items (short):
- Jonah: Open Dedicated burst request (link JIRA-1228) and add expected windows + instance types. ETA 11/05.
- Marina: Confirm demo GPU slot schedule and whether demos can run off-hosted cheaper cache. ETA 11/06.
- Ethan: Update canary autoscale policy to allow short 3x burst; coordinate SRE. ETA 11/05.
- Sophia: Confirm enterprise pilot start date and consult with Private infra to reserve nodes. ETA 11/04.
- Carlos: Add job tagging for background-evals so we can throttle during peak. ETA 11/05.

Open questions / blockers (callouts):
- Dedicated burst approval SLA: can we get approval within 24 hours? If not, fallback plan = reduce canary duration or run smaller batch sizes.
- Private node procurement lead time if hardware is required — raised to infra team but needs answer.
- Observability ingestion cost if tracing ingestion spikes; need to define throttling thresholds.

Notes / context links:
- JIRA-1228: Dedicated burst request (Jonah).
- JIRA-1367: Enterprise pilot setup (Sophia).
- Confluence quick playbook link above for burst runbook and post-mortem template.

How to use this doc: Paste the table into a shared sheet, have owners fill actual expected GPUs, and re-run the quick math. We'll keep this doc as the ephemeral single-source for the initial decision meeting on 2026-11-05 10:00 PT.

Changelog (quick):
- 2026-11-02 Aisha: created initial mosaic with rough numbers.
- 2026-11-03 Jonah: updated hosted-inference numbers after slimmable models tests.
- 2026-11-04 Sophia: added enterprise-pilot estimated needs and clarified isolation ask.

Notes to self (informal):
- If Dedicated pool can't cover, consider spilling lower-priority workloads to preemptive spot instances or delay non-customer-facing evals.
- Keep communications tight: short Slack channel (#burst-ops) and update this doc only for numbers/asks to avoid confusion.
